eastmanosteus:enwiki:6.title: Eastmanosteus (E. lundarensis Hanke, Stewart and Lammers, 1996)

facts.statement: Eastmanosteus is a fossil genus of placoderms belonging to the group Dunkleostea.
facts.quote: Eastmanosteus ("Eastman's bone") is a fossil genus of dunkleosteid placoderms.

facts.statement: Eastmanosteus fossils are found in marine sediments from the Middle to Late Devonian periods across many parts of the world.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in many parts of the world in marine sediments dating from the Middle to Late Devonian.

facts.statement: Eastmanosteus were medium-to-large fish, with some specimens reaching nearly 3 meters in total length.
facts.quote: They were medium-to-large fish, with specimens E. pustulosus and E. licharevi approaching a total length of 3 m.

facts.statement: Complete exoskeletons with preserved soft-tissue traces of E. calliaspis from Australia make this species one of the best-known dunkleosteids.
facts.quote: Complete exoskeletons with soft-tissue traces of E. calliaspis from Australia make this one of the best known dunkleosteids.

facts.statement: The genus Eastmanosteus was described by Obruchev in 1964.
The type species of the genus Eastmanosteus is Dinichthys pustulosus.
Eastmanosteus and its relative Dunkleosteus belong to the family Dunkleosteidae.
facts.quote: Eastmanosteus and its relative Dunkleosteus belong to the family Dunkleosteidae.

facts.statement: A 2016 study suggests that the status of Dunkleosteidae as a clade separate from Dunkleosteoidea is in doubt.
facts.quote: Alternatively, the subsequent 2016 Zhu et al. study using a larger morphological dataset recovered Panxiosteidae well outside of Dunkleosteoidea, leaving the status of Dunkleosteidae as a clade grouping separate from Dunkleosteoidea in doubt

facts.statement: E. calliaspis fossils come from the Frasnian Gogo Formation in northwestern Western Australia.
facts.quote: From the Frasnian Gogo Formation of northwestern Western Australia.

facts.statement: E. licharevi is a poorly known species from Russia, with material from the Frasnian and Famennian periods.
facts.quote: A poorly known species from Russia, originally described from an isolated nuchal plate from the Frasnian of Timman with additional material from the Famennian of Lipetsk.

facts.statement: E. lundarensis is a medium-sized species from the Eifelian period of south-central Manitoba, Canada.
facts.quote: A medium-sized species from the Eifelian of south-central Manitoba, Canada.

facts.statement: E. pustulosus was a large, widely distributed form found in the Middle-Late Devonian of the United States and the Frasnian of Poland.
facts.quote: It was a large and widely distributed form, with fossil material from the Middle-Late Devonian of the United Stastes (Wisconsin, Iowa, Michigan, New York state) and the Frasnian of Poland.

facts.statement: E. yunnanensis is from the Middle Devonian of Yunnan Province, China.
facts.quote: Originally assigned to Dunkleosteus. From the Middle Devonian of Yunnan Province, China.

facts.statement: An undescribed species of Eastmanosteus is based on material from the Frasnian of Kerman, east Iran.
facts.quote: An undescribed species based on relatively well-preserved material from the Frasnian of Kerman, east Iran.

facts.statement: The time range for Eastmanosteus is from the Givetian to the Frasnian, approximately 387.95 to 375.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Givetian to Frasnian (387.95 to 375.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Eastmanosteus is classified in the class Placodermi.

rejected.statement: Eastmanosteus was closely related to Dunkleosteus but differed in size, having a tuberculated bone ornament, a differently shaped nuchal plate, and a zig-zagging skull roof suture pattern.
rejected.quote: It was closely related to the giant Dunkleosteus, but differed from that genus in size and in possessing a distinctive tuberculated bone ornament, a differently shaped nuchal plate, and a more zig-zagging course of the sutures of the skull roof.

rejected.statement: Eastmanosteus species possessed powerful jaws with sharp cutting edges and were likely active predators.
rejected.quote: Species of Eastmanosteus had powerful jaws with sharp cutting edges and were likely active predators.
